findings.title: Polymarket Halts Trading After Reports of Stolen Funds (Bloomberg)
findings.summary_md: Bloomberg reported on October 29, 2026 that Polymarket stopped trading on its international exchange after a third-party software provider was compromised. The article noted user reports of lost funds and identified the vendor compromise as the root cause. It was among the earliest news reports of the incident, published before the story's first_seen timestamp.

findings.title: CNBC: Polymarket Reports Outage on International Exchange
findings.summary_md: CNBC covered the October 29 incident, reporting that some Polymarket international users had funds stolen due to a hack of an unnamed third-party provider. The company halted trading and referred the matter to UK authorities. The report preceded the engine's first_seen timestamp of October 30.

findings.title: Cyber Kendra: Polymarket Hacked via DebugBear Script
findings.summary_md: Cyber Kendra reported that researchers linked the theft to malicious JavaScript served from DebugBear, a UK-based performance monitoring firm. The article cited Hudson Rock's analysis of a payload that hunted for logged-in trading sessions and moved proceeds to an attacker-controlled wallet. Published October 29, before the engine's first_seen date.

findings.title: BleepingComputer: Crypto-Draining Script Breach
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer detailed the supply-chain attack on October 29, noting Hudson Rock found malicious code from a DebugBear address used by Polymarket. The payload read credential-related material and targeted trading sessions. The article cited a production commit message removing the DebugBear RUM script, confirming the vendor as the entry point.
